overview: Memeware 7.3's Stealer empties chests with one shift-click per delay period: while a GuiChest is open it walks the container slots and window-clicks the first slot holding a stack every Delay ticks (default 4, so 5 clicks per second), emits C0D through the fork's closeScreen when the chest looks empty, and in Nearby mode scans a 7x7x7 box for chests, swings with C0A and right-clicks them open with C08. The per-tick gating is the modulo of the player's tick counter against the rounded Delay setting, which also means a Delay of 0 divides by zero and crashes the client the first tick the handler runs. The emptied-chest list is cleared on every S08 teleport and on enable, so the module re-opens chests after a respawn or teleport.

sections.p: The first consumer handles the open-chest case. When mc.currentScreen is a GuiChest, the module checks the container for items by scanning the first 27 or 54 slots depending on the slot count (90 slots means a double chest), and while anything remains it iterates the slot list and shift-clicks the first occupied slot through mc.playerController.windowClick with mode 1, one click per handler run. The click fires only when ticksExisted modulo the rounded Delay equals zero, so the pacing is a fixed 20 divided by Delay clicks per second, not a timer. When the container is empty, the Close setting (on by default) or Nearby mode closes the screen with mc.displayGuiScreen(null), which the fork's EntityPlayerSP.closeScreen turns into a C0DPacketCloseWindow with the open window id.

Nearby mode is the second behavior: with no screen open, every Delay ticks it scans a 7x7x7 block box around the player, and for each BlockChest within a distance-squared of 16 that is not in the emptiedChests list it adds the position, sends a C0APacketAnimation swing through PacketUtil, and calls onPlayerRightClick with the DOWN facing, which makes the fork's PlayerControllerMP emit the C08 use-item packet that opens the chest. The emptied list is cleared by the second consumer on every S08PacketPlayerPosLook after terrain load and on every enable, so chests are only opened once per position per teleport. The scan order is y from 3 down to -3, then x and z ascending, so nearer chests win ties.

The fork's PlayerControllerMP.windowClick builds only C0EPacketClickWindow (slot id, button, mode, the clicked stack and the container's next transaction id) and never calls syncCurrentPlayItem, so the shift-clicks emit pure C0E with no C09 held-item sync, and the module never changes the held item anyway. The close path emits C0D, and the Nearby open path emits C0A plus C08. The Delay modulo gating means the packet rate is deterministic: Delay 4 is 5 C0E per second, Delay 2 is 10, Delay 1 is 20, and Delay 0 is a client crash, because ticksExisted modulo zero throws. The S08 consumer runs on the receive side and only clears the list, so a teleport mid-steal resets the open-set without touching the open chest.

files.label: Stealer.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is two registered consumers plus a small container helper. eventConsumer0 is the steal loop: the open-chest branch shift-clicks the first occupied slot when the tick modulo passes, and the Nearby branch scans for chests, swings with C0A and right-clicks them open. eventConsumer1 clears the emptied-chest list on S08 teleports, and isEmpty counts occupied slots among the first 27 or 54 to decide when the drain is done. The Delay setting gates everything through the tick modulo, which is the module's rate control and its crash edge at zero.\n\nThe Close boolean and the mode string are the only other settings, and the class never touches timers or packet buffers; every effect on the wire is one of the three fork paths described above. The import of the lwjeb @Handler registration is the client's event wiring, and the module binds itself to the UpdateEvent and PacketInEvent buses through it.

files.label: PlayerControllerMP.java (fork window protocol)
files.explanation: The fork's PlayerControllerMP defines every packet the module puts on the wire. windowClick computes the container's next transaction id, runs slotClick locally to get the clicked stack, and queues a single C0EPacketClickWindow; notably it never calls syncCurrentPlayItem, so window clicks carry no C09 held-item sync, a fork fingerprint that the module inherits. onPlayerRightClick is the chest-open path: for an activated block it queues the C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with the position, facing and held stack that the Nearby mode triggers, and onStoppedUsingItem and the other sync sites show where C09 would come from in vanilla.\n\nThe module calls only windowClick and onPlayerRightClick, so this one file accounts for the entire C0E and C08 footprint. The C0D close comes from the fork's EntityPlayerSP.closeScreen rather than this class, and the C0A swing is sent directly by the module. Reading the fork file is what proves the no-C09 claim instead of assuming vanilla behavior.

countering.label: FastClick (window click rate)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus FastClick scores InventoryClickEvent traffic into an ActionFrequency with five 200ms buckets: the newest bucket is compared against the short-term limit of 4 and the full window against the normal limit of 15, with TickTask lag division before the comparison. A plain shift-click with an empty cursor counts 1.0 via getAmountWithAction. The check also carries the container-interaction path: any click landing within the 155ms min-interaction-duration default after the container opened adds a violation of (155 / duration) * 100, and slot -999 throws are excluded entirely.\n\nThe stock configuration is the honest gap: Delay 4 is exactly 5 clicks per second, one per 200ms bucket and 5 across the window, safely under both limits, so a default drain passes the rate paths. The pressure comes from the dial and the open: Delay 1 raises the rate to 20 per second, blowing the 15 window (about 5 VL per click, cancel at vl>150 within about 1.5 seconds), and the first click always lands within a frame of the chest opening because there is no first-delay setting, so the interact_time path scores close to 100 VL on every drain regardless of the delay. The module's tick-modulo pacing is rigid, which is exactly what a bucket check is built to fingerprint.

countering.label: Open (inventory close on movement)
countering.explanation: NCP's Open check watches PlayerMoveEvent traffic while an inventory window is open. checkOnMove skips duplicate packets, vehicles, creative quickbar clicks, merchants and velocity-affected moves, then decides whether the move carries an impulse: with modern input it reads the WASD/jump bits directly, otherwise it falls back to the movement model's hasImpulse decision. An impulse while open feeds Improbable and returns true, and the caller force-closes the inventory, resetting inventoryOpenTime and containerInteractTime.\n\nThe module suppresses nothing, so any strafing or stepping during a drain is visible to the check and a single impulse move mid-steal closes the chest and aborts the session. The practical tension is the same as every stealer: a still player never trips it, so the check is a soft counter that converts a movement mistake into a lost window and resets the open-time baseline FastClick's interact_time path reads. The Nearby mode's walking between chests happens with no window open and is invisible to it.

countering.label: InventoryActions (window state mismatch)
countering.explanation: Hawk's InventoryActions punishes world interaction while a window is open and, more importantly for stealers, punishes ClickInventoryEvent packets when HawkPlayer.hasInventoryOpen() is zero. Hawk derives the open state from the S2D window-open, C16 inventory command and close packets, so it tracks the server's window lifecycle, not the client's GUI state, and every punish calls e.resync().\n\nThe module's close-then-reopen cadence is the race surface. The empty-chest branch calls mc.displayGuiScreen(null), which queues C0D, and in Nearby mode the next delay tick can immediately right-click another chest and swing; if Hawk has not yet processed the C0D, the C0A swing and C08 open arrive while hasInventoryOpen is still non-zero and are punished and resynced. The reverse edge is equally live: a click that lands after the server-side close processed arrives with the window flag at zero and is punished as a click on a closed window. The emptiedChests list gives no cover because the check is content-blind and window-id aware.

countering.label: FastConsume (eat-duration; silent for stealers)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's FastConsume guards the item-use path of the inventory family. The inventory listener stamps a consume time on the right-click of an edible or potion, and the check compares it against the consume-time limit (1280ms default) when PlayerItemConsumeEvent fires, flagging any consume that completes faster than a real eat could. The mechanism only engages when a consume event actually lands, which requires the full vanilla use duration to elapse.\n\nFor this module the check is silent by design: shift-click C0E traffic, the C0D close and the Nearby C08 opens never produce a consume event, so FastConsume stays quiet through an entire drain. The entry belongs in the set because the same C0E corpus pools the eat-rate checks with the click-rate checks, and it documents the boundary honestly: the real pressure on this module is FastClick's click ledger, while FastConsume is the guard for the instant-consume sibling modules, which would trip it on any server that processes eats immediately.
